To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a significant proportion of the Nepalese population have high baseline titers to S. entericaserotypes Typhi O and Typhi H antigens and therefore a new cut off value for diagnosis of entericfever is needed.

the baseline antibody titers of 12.5% and 6% of the healthy individuals against S. entericaserotypes Typhi and Paratyphi A, respectively, were ≥ 1:160, and that the baseline titers of 3% and 2% of the healthy volunteers against S. entericaserotypes Paratyphi B and S. entericasubsp. arizonae were ≥ 1/160.
the cutoff levels for the diagnosis of S. enterica enteric fever using the Widal agglutation test in Nepal should be changed to ≥ 1:160 anti-H titer and ≥ 1.80 anti-O titer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of a baseline titer against S. enterice in Nepal.
the distribution of antibody titer in apparently healthy population and its implications in the diagnosis of enterica fever.
the baseline titers of antibodies against S. enteric serotypes Typhi and Paratyphi A, B in healthy individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the currently used cutoff values of 1:20 for both "O" and H antigens of S. enterica Typhi and "O" antigen of S. entericaserotype Paratyphi A are inappropriate and should be revised to > 1 : 80 for anti-O titer and > 1 :160 for anti-H titer of S. entericeaserotype Typhi.
the cutoff levels for Widal test should be > 1:20 for all antigens of S. enterica.
the cutoff values of 1:20 and 1:40 for anti-O and anti-H titers, respectively, against S. enteria serotype Typhi would be appropriate for the diagnosis of typhoid fever in Nepal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cutoff values of Widal test for diagnosis of enteric fevers in Nepal are 1:80 (O) and 1:160 (H) for S. typhi and 1:40 (O) and > 1/20 (H) for other serotypes of Salmonella enteric.
a single Widal titer should not be used to diagnose enteric fever in Nepal and the currently used cutoff values should be revised.
the cutoff levels for the Widal agglutation test in Nepal would be >1:80 for the anti-O titer and > 1.60 for the anti-H titer for serotype Typhi.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cutoff levels for enteric fever diagnosis should not be uniform across all regions.
the currently used cutoffs for the Widal aggluination test in Nepal are likely not appropriate.
a single Widal test should be used with caution to diagnose enteric fever in Nepal and other countries with a similar epidemiology.
